title: Countdown to Launch
story: The rocket is on the launchpad. Mission Control starts the countdown: 10... 9... 8... Every second, one number appears on the giant screen. When it hits zero � BLAST OFF! Your program can be Mission Control, counting down from any number you choose.
why: `while` loops are how programs repeat an action until something changes. They power everything from game countdowns to loading bars to video playback.
analogy: A countdown loop is like a staircase � you start at the top step, take one step down each time through the loop, and stop when you reach the ground floor.
try_it: Start the countdown from 20 instead of 10. Then try counting down from 3. What happens if you start at 0? (Hint: the loop body runs zero times!) Can you add '...' after each number to make it look more dramatic?
tips: Use `var` (not `let`) for the count variable � it needs to change inside the loop.
The condition is checked BEFORE each loop iteration. If it's false from the start, the loop runs zero times.
Always make sure your loop makes progress toward the condition being false � otherwise you get an infinite loop.
You can print anything inside the loop � add dots, messages, or even multiple lines per count.
common_mistakes: Using `let` instead of `var`: `let count = 10;` then `count = count - 1;` will fail because `let` variables can't change.
Forgetting to subtract inside the loop � the count never changes, so the loop runs forever.
Putting a semicolon after the while condition: `while count > 0; {` � the semicolon creates an empty loop body.
Using `<=` instead of `>`: `while count <= 0` when count starts at 10 � condition is false immediately, loop never runs.
